description: The plot illustrates the loss of various large language models over the number of iterations. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration", has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 140000, and has tick labels at intervals of 20000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss", has a linear scale, and ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot displays six lines representing different models: Vanilla (purple, solid), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid), and SepLLM (n=128) (navy blue, solid). All lines start at a high loss value around 3.4 at 0 iterations and decrease as the number of iterations increases, with the Vanilla model starting at the highest loss and StrmLLM (n=64) having the highest loss among the models at 140000 iterations, at approximately 2.65. The other four SepLLM models have loss values ranging from approximately 2.5 to 2.55 at 140000 iterations, with SepLLM (n=128) having the lowest loss. The lines generally decrease rapidly in the initial 20000 iterations, then continue to decrease at a slower rate until 140000 iterations.
